question: Assume today is 2026-09-05. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of new passenger cars (Pkw) registered in Germany in September 2026, as it will be first reported in the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt's (KBA) monthly press release on vehicle registrations.

target.what: New passenger cars (Personenkraftwagen, Pkw) newly registered in Germany during September 2026, as counted by the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt (KBA) in its monthly vehicle-registration statistics and first reported in the KBA monthly press release. Counts each new Pkw registration event in the domestic Germ
target.cadence: monthly; first preliminary monthly result for September 2026, normally published in early October 2026
target.caveats: At the 2026-09-05 cutoff the target month is almost entirely future and no KBA September 2026 monthly result exists yet. The target is domestic new Pkw registrations, not sales, orders, production, exports, or total motor-vehicle registrations. KBA Pkw definition and any later revisions can differ f

candidates.hypothesis: September 2026 Pkw registrations should be anchored by the recent monthly run-rate scaled by the historical September seasonal factor and recent year-over-year momentum. This is the primary direct route: target ≈ recent run-rate × September seasonal multiplier × trend adjustment.
candidates.data_to_find: KBA monthly Pkw Neuzulassungen totals for January 2019 through August 2026, especially September 2019-September 2025 and the latest available August 2026 figure; calendar working days; private/commercial and powertrain splits if available. Minimum needed: a consistent monthly total series and enough September observations to estimate a seasonal factor. Substitute: KBA annual totals plus monthly shares.
search_hints: Pkw Neuzulassungen Monat September historisch KBA

candidates.perspective: German auto-market forecast and annual-total analyst
candidates.hypothesis: The September 2026 count can be derived as forecast 2026 annual Pkw registrations × the historical September share of the annual total, with adjustment for year-to-date over/underperformance. A credible annual forecast constrains the level even without September-specific data.
candidates.data_to_find: Published 2026 German passenger-car registration forecasts available by 2026-09-05 (VDA, ifo, industry associations, government or bank research); KBA January-August 2026 year-to-date actual Pkw registrations; historical September share of annual Pkw registrations, ideally 2015-2025. Minimum: one 2026 annual forecast and a usable September share.
search_hints: Pkw Neuzulassungen Januar bis August 2026 KBA

candidates.hypothesis: German September registrations can be benchmarked against ACEA/EU monthly passenger-car registration data and peer-market September seasonality. If German August 2026 and prior September values are known, a comparable-market seasonal ratio or EU growth rate can validate or adjust the direct KBA-history route.
candidates.data_to_find: ACEA monthly new passenger-car registrations for Germany and the EU/EFTA from January 2024 to August 2026, plus September 2024 and September 2025; peer-country September seasonal ratios. Minimum: German and EU September observations and the latest August 2026 German figure.
search_hints: ACEA new passenger car registrations Germany August 2026
ACEA September 2025 passenger car registrations Germany
EU car registrations monthly September seasonality ACEA

candidates.hypothesis: Known policy and macroeconomic shocks change September 2026 registrations mainly through pull-forward and demand timing: EV purchase incentives or taxes, company-car taxation, EU CO2 fleet rules, interest rates, fuel prices, consumer confidence, and announced regulatory changes. The direction depends on whether a change creates a rush before or a payback after the effective date.
candidates.data_to_find: German and EU passenger-car policy changes effective in 2025-2026 that were announced by 2026-09-05, especially EV subsidies, company-car benefit-in-kind taxation, CO2 fleet targets, and registration-tax rules; German consumer confidence, ECB policy rates, car price index, and fuel prices for August 2026. Minimum: a dated list of material policy changes plus one demand indicator.

candidates.hypothesis: Domestic registrations require delivered vehicles, so passenger-car production, exports, order backlog, dealer inventory, and delivery times can constrain or signal the September count. Production is not registrations because exports and inventory changes intervene, but severe supply constraints or order backlogs shift timing.
candidates.data_to_find: VDA and Statistisches Bundesamt monthly German passenger-car production, exports, and domestic sales for January-August 2026; ifo order backlog and business climate for autos; dealer inventory or delivery-time indicators. Minimum: latest production and order-backlog observations plus a bridge assumption from supply to domestic registrations.

candidates.hypothesis: The monthly count is the sum of daily registration events across German Kfz-Zulassungsstellen and online registration channels. Capacity is usually not binding, but appointment capacity, working days, public holidays, IT outages, and end-of-month bunching affect timing and can shift registrations between months.
candidates.data_to_find: Number and capacity of German vehicle registration offices, daily appointment throughput, online/direct registration volumes, public holidays and school holidays in September 2026, and any known KBA or registration-office disruptions before the cutoff. Minimum: a daily-capacity estimate and September 2026 working-day calendar. Substitute: national working-day count and historical daily-average registration rate.

candidates.hypothesis: September Pkw registrations can be decomposed into private and commercial/fleet registrations. Commercial/fleet registrations respond to business confidence and fleet-replacement cycles; private registrations respond to consumer confidence and incentives. Combining stable segment shares with leading indicators can produce an independent estimate: target = private + commercial.
candidates.data_to_find: KBA monthly private versus commercial Pkw registration shares from 2024 to August 2026; ifo business climate; German consumer confidence; fleet order or company-car registration indicators; rental and large-fleet registration timing. Minimum: recent segment shares plus one indicator for each segment.
search_hints: KBA Pkw Neuzulassungen gewerblich privat August 2026

candidates.hypothesis: Daily registration rates vary by weekday and month-end effects. September 2026 total can be built from weekday-specific daily rates or adjusted from a monthly average using the exact weekday composition and public holidays. This constrains any run-rate route rather than standing alone.
candidates.data_to_find: Exact September 2026 calendar, weekday counts, German public holidays and school-holiday periods, bridge days, and historical KBA September observations aligned to weekday composition. Minimum: September 2026 weekday count and historical daily-average pattern by weekday or a simple working-day adjustment.

directions.hypothesis: If the 2026 EV purchase subsidy actually closes or changes its application rules around 2026-09-30, September 2026 will contain a policy-driven pull-forward of BEV deliveries, making the high BEV-momentum route m5 more representative and the pure seasonal routes m1/m4 too low. Confirming that no such deadline exists would instead support treating p202's 2026-09-30 period as page validity rather than a programme end.
directions.data_to_find: Official BAFA/BMUV programme rules and application deadline for the 2026 German EV purchase subsidy, plus any KBA or VDA commentary on September 2026 EV pull-forward.

directions.hypothesis: Monthly KBA Pkw registrations for October-December 2025 (and 2024) would let us estimate the September share of the September-December remainder directly instead of assuming a1 in route m3. This is the largest avoidable uncertainty in the annual-forecast route.
directions.data_to_find: KBA monthly new Pkw registration totals for October, November, and December 2025 and, if possible, the same months of 2024.

directions.hypothesis: September 2026 has 22 working days and no nationwide holiday. Confirming August 2026 and September 2025 working-day counts and, ideally, September 2025 daily registration bunching would validate whether the historical September-over-August MoM changes in m4 are distorted by calendar differences. This would sharpen the seasonal route rather than replace it.
directions.data_to_find: Working-day counts for August 2026 and August/September 2025, and any KBA daily or weekday-level September 2025 registration data.

assessment.note: All report the same KBA September 2025 total of 235,528 Pkw. They are duplicate renderings of one underlying measurement, not independent confirmations. p1 is the canonical kept level used in methods.
All report the same January-September 2025 cumulative total of 2,110,348 Pkw. Same KBA/VDIK source, so duplicate rather than independent evidence. p2 is kept for the seasonal-ratio route.
All state September 2025 was +12.8% year on year. This is consistent with p1 and p45 but not an independent measurement.
All state September 2025 was +13.7% versus August 2025. p4 is kept as the 2025 September-over-August seasonal change.
All report September 2024 total Pkw registrations of 208,848. p45 is the canonical KBA value kept for the two-year seasonal-ratio and MoM checks.
January-September 2024 cumulative Pkw registrations, used with p45 to form the January-August 2024 denominator for the seasonal-ratio route.
Both report August 2026 total Pkw registrations of 212,563. p30 is the canonical kept August 2026 level.
p31 gives August 2026 year-on-year growth as +2.6%; the VDA table rounds this to 3%. The difference is rounding, not a material conflict. p31 is kept as recent total-market momentum.
All report July 2026 Pkw registrations of 268,068. Duplicate KBA figures from different publications.
Both report July 2026 Pkw registrations +1.2% versus July 2025. p475 is kept as recent market momentum.
August 2026 BEV registrations of 68,930 and a 32.4% BEV share are mutually consistent and come from KBA-derived reporting. p32 is kept for the powertrain-momentum route.

August 2026 BEV registrations were +75.1% year on year, while domestic BEV order intake was +62% in August and +64% year to date. Orders are not registrations, but the direction strongly supports elevated BEV momentum rather than weak demand.

All reflect the same VDA forecast of about 2.90 million German Pkw registrations in 2026. These are duplicate publications of one forecast, not independent market observations. p84 is kept for the annual-forecast route.

These describe the 2026 German EV purchase subsidy design. They are policy context, not September 2026 registration counts. p202's stated period ending 2026-09-30 is ambiguous against p139's 2026-2029 programme window and may reflect page validity rather than a programme deadline; I do not treat it as a confirmed pull-forward deadline without confirmation.

The calendar sources agree that September 2026 has 30 calendar days, 22 Monday-Friday working days, and no nationwide public holiday. This supports the ordinary-seasonality assumption but does not by itself give a registration level.

August 2026 production, exports, and domestic order intake are not registrations. They are useful context: production/exports were not obviously supply-collapsed, and domestic order intake was positive, especially for BEVs. The conversion from production/orders to September registrations is not direct.

p101 is labelled as January-August 2025 but equals the January-September 2025 cumulative total, so it is an erroneous derived value. p102 is labelled as a share but its value is a monthly registration count. Both are inconsistent with p1/p2 and unusable.
p185 gives a 0.2% BEV share for 2025, which contradicts its own quote saying about one-fifth and the surrounding BEV evidence. It is a typographical/unit error.
These are total motor-vehicle (Kfz) registrations across all vehicle classes, not Pkw registrations. Definitional scope differs from the target.
These are commercial-vehicle (Nutzfahrzeuge) registrations, not passenger cars.
These are average CO2 emissions of new Pkw, not registration counts.
These are used-car ownership transfers, not new Pkw registrations.

extra_directions.hypothesis: If the 2026 EV purchase subsidy actually closes or changes its application rules around 2026-09-30, September 2026 will contain a policy-driven pull-forward of BEV deliveries, making the high BEV-momentum route m5 more representative and the pure seasonal routes m1/m4 too low. Confirming that no such deadline exists would instead support treating p202's 2026-09-30 period as page validity rather than a programme end.
extra_directions.data_to_find: Official BAFA/BMUV programme rules and application deadline for the 2026 German EV purchase subsidy, plus any KBA or VDA commentary on September 2026 EV pull-forward.

extra_directions.hypothesis: Monthly KBA Pkw registrations for October-December 2025 (and 2024) would let us estimate the September share of the September-December remainder directly instead of assuming a1 in route m3. This is the largest avoidable uncertainty in the annual-forecast route.
extra_directions.data_to_find: KBA monthly new Pkw registration totals for October, November, and December 2025 and, if possible, the same months of 2024.

extra_directions.hypothesis: September 2026 has 22 working days and no nationwide holiday. Confirming August 2026 and September 2025 working-day counts and, ideally, September 2025 daily registration bunching would validate whether the historical September-over-August MoM changes in m4 are distorted by calendar differences. This would sharpen the seasonal route rather than replace it.
extra_directions.data_to_find: Working-day counts for August 2026 and August/September 2025, and any KBA daily or weekday-level September 2025 registration data.

p297.role: January-August 2026 cumulative new Pkw registrations in Germany, the observed current-year base

p1.role: September 2025 new Pkw registrations in Germany

p2.role: January-September 2025 cumulative new Pkw registrations; p2 minus p1 is the January-August 2025 base

p45.role: September 2024 new Pkw registrations in Germany

p46.role: January-September 2024 cumulative new Pkw registrations; p46 minus p45 is the January-August 2024 base

methods.rationale: Seasonal YTD-ratio route: apply the historical September share of the January-August cumulative to the observed January-August 2026 total. Averaging 2024 and 2025 reduces one-year seasonal noise. It assumes the KBA Pkw definition and September timing pattern are comparable across years. Failure modes: a September 2026 policy pull-forward, a change in end-of-quarter registration bunching, or revisions to p2/p46. p1 and p2 share a source, as do p45 and p46, so the ratio uncertainties are partly correlated.

methods.rationale: Momentum route: carry the average July-August 2026 year-on-year growth into September 2026, applied to the September 2025 level. It assumes recent total-market momentum persists and that the September 2025 base is a suitable seasonal anchor. Failure modes: September year-on-year growth diverges from July-August because of BEV subsidy timing, model launches, or calendar effects. p1 also appears in m5 and p31 in m4/m5, so these routes are not fully independent.

methods.rationale: Annual-forecast allocation route: subtract observed January-August 2026 registrations from the VDA 2026 annual forecast, then allocate the four-month remainder to September using a1. It constrains the level independently of the recent monthly seasonal ratios but depends on the forecast still being valid and on an explicit September share assumption. Failure modes: stale VDA forecast, a September policy pull-forward, or an unusual Q4 phasing. It shares p297 with m1 but not the seasonal history.

methods.rationale: Powertrain-momentum route: split September 2025 into BEV and non-BEV, apply August 2026's BEV year-on-year growth to BEV, and apply August 2026's implied non-BEV year-on-year growth to non-BEV. This explicitly captures the current BEV surge and the simultaneous non-BEV decline. Failure modes: August BEV growth mean-reverts or accelerates sharply in September, the non-BEV decline changes, or p32/p30/p31 are revised. It shares p1 and p31 with m2 and p30 with m4, so it is not an independent confirmation of those routes.

assumptions.name: September share of September-December 2026 Pkw registrations implied by the annual forecast
assumptions.rationale: The VDA annual forecast p84 (2.90 million) minus January-August actual p297 (1,965,024) leaves a September-December remainder. September is one of four months and is typically similar to or slightly above the average Q4 month; a 25% share is a neutral central allocation, with a wide 22-28% range because no kept point supplies 2025 October-December monthly totals.
assumptions.applies_when: The VDA 2.90 million annual forecast remains a reasonable anchor for full-year 2026 and September 2026 is not distorted by an unobserved subsidy deadline or other one-off pull-forward.
assumptions.falsified_by: A confirmed September 2026 policy deadline causing abnormal pull-forward, a material VDA forecast revision after June 2026, or 2025 October-December data showing September's share of the four-month remainder far outside 22-28%.

assessment.note: All report the same KBA/VDIK September 2025 total of 235,528 Pkw. They are repeated publications of the same underlying KBA measurement, not independent confirmations.
All report September 2024 Pkw registrations at 208,848, the prior-year September level.
Same January-September 2025 cumulative Pkw total, 2,110,348. Together with p1 it implies the January-August 2025 base used in the seasonal-share route.

September-over-August changes of +13.7% in 2025 and +5.8% in 2024 support a positive September seasonal step, but the two years had different working-day compositions, so the raw ratios are only approximate.
Both p30 and p296 give August 2026 total Pkw registrations of 212,563; p31 gives the corresponding +2.6% year-on-year change. These come from the same KBA monthly release.
August 2026 BEV count, share and year-on-year growth are internally consistent: 68,930 BEV, 32.4% share, +75.1% versus August 2025.
July 2026 KBA data agree on 268,068 Pkw, +1.2% year-on-year, and cumulative January-July 2026 of 1,752,461.
January-August 2026 cumulative total of 1,965,024 is the VDA/KBA observed current-year base and is consistent with p30 as the August component.
These are the same VDA 2026 forecast: about 2.90 million new Pkw registrations, +2% versus 2025. Repeated citations are not independent forecasts.

KBA monthly releases for September-December 2025 give the historical September share of the September-December remainder. Same publisher and overlapping annual total, so this is one seasonal-distribution source.

The 2026 German EV purchase programme parameters are consistent: base BEV 3,000 EUR, PHEV/range-extender 1,500 EUR, maximum up to 6,000 EUR. p202's stated period ending 2026-09-30 is a stale page-validity date, not evidence of a programme end, because p508 dated 2026-09-03 describes the programme as running 2026-2029.
The subsidy application window and 2026-2029 programme horizon indicate no known 30 September 2026 subsidy deadline, so September 2026 should not be treated as a policy-cliff pull-forward month.
Company-car benefit-in-kind rules for electric cars remain favourable through 2030, and plug-in hybrids face 0.5% only if range/CO2 criteria are met. No September 2026 tax change is evident.
EU CO2 fleet rules are in a 2025-2027 flexibility period and do not create a September 2026 registration deadline.
September 2026 has 22 working days and no nationwide statutory holiday; August 2026 has 21 working days. State-level counts agree with the national calendar.

August 2026 German Pkw production was 229,900 and exports 168,300, so domestic registrations cannot be equated with production minus exports because imports and inventory changes intervene. Domestic BEV orders +62% in August and +64% year-to-date corroborate strong BEV momentum.

The market remains about 21% below the 2019 level after eight months, and the August 2026 private share rose to 40.5% with EV support. This is useful context for private/BEV strength, not a direct September total.

methods.rationale: Direct seasonal-share route, unchanged from round 1: it applies the average historical September-to-January-August ratio (2025 and 2024) to the observed January-August 2026 cumulative. Shared dependency: p297 comes from the same KBA/VDA current-year series as p30 and appears also in the team's other routes; p1 and p45 are historical KBA September values. methods.rationale: Year-on-year momentum route, unchanged from round 1: September 2025 carried forward by the average recent total-market growth of July and August 2026. It shares p1 with the seasonal routes and p31 with the BEV/non-BEV decomposition, so it is not independent confirmation of them. Failure modes: the +2.6% August change is itself a raw, unadjusted year-on-year figure that includes a working-day difference versus August 2025, and late-summer momentum may not persist; because September 2026 and September 2025 both have 22 working days, no further calendar correction is applied.

p558.role: Full-year 2025 German new Pkw registrations, an annual total, the realised base of the forecast's growth rate

methods.rationale: Annual-forecast route, repaired. The round-1 version subtracted an eight-month cumulative (p297) from an annual forecast (p84) without aligning units or periods and then multiplied by a September share of the September-December remainder; that made the residual unit-inconsistent and produced a result an order of magnitude below the other routes. The repaired version keeps the same idea (let the annual forecast constrain the level) but uses only quantities with a coherent period: September 2025 multiplied by the forecast's implied annual growth factor, forecast 2026 total divided by the realised 2025 total (about +1.5%). Shared dependencies: p84 is a forecast, not an outcome, made in mid-2026 before the observed August weakness, and p1 is shared with m1, m2, m4 and m5. Failure modes: the forecast predates the second half of 2026 and looks slightly conservative given year-to-date 2026 registrations (p297) running about 4.8% above the same eight months of 2025, so this route sits at the lower end of the set.

methods.rationale: Month-over-month seasonal route, unchanged from round 1: the observed August 2026 total times the average historical September-over-August change from 2025 (+13.7%) and 2024 (+5.8%). Shared dependency: p30 is also the anchor of the BEV/non-BEV route m5. Failure modes: the two historical changes differ by a factor of more than two because they mix seasonality with working-day and holiday timing (September 2025 had one extra working day versus its prior year, per p18), so the average is a noisy seasonal factor; the wide spread is why this route is not treated as precise.

methods.rationale: BEV/non-BEV decomposition route, unchanged from round 1: September 2025's BEV and non-BEV stocks are grown separately, BEV by the latest August 2026 BEV growth (+75.1%) and non-BEV by the implied August 2026 non-BEV year-on-year factor recovered from totals and BEV counts. Shared dependencies: p1, p30, p31, p32 and p34 come from the same KBA August/September releases, so they are not independent measurements. Failure modes: the 75% BEV growth is extreme and may not persist into September, and the recovered non-BEV decline may be an August timing artefact; the 2026-2029 purchase subsidy appears to be running with no confirmed end-September deadline, which argues against a policy cliff, but demand payback after heavy BEV pull-forward remains possible.

final.template:
The best estimate for new passenger car (Pkw) registrations in Germany during September 2026 is [[estimate]] [[unit]] ([[interval_level]] interval [[p10]] to [[p90]] [[unit]]). This covers domestic new Pkw registration events counted by the KBA for the full month, not sales, orders, or production.

Evidence: September 2025 was [[p1_value]]; January–August 2026 cumulative was [[p297_value]]; August 2026 was [[p30_value]] with year-on-year growth of [[p31_value]]. Routes apply historical September shares, recent momentum, a VDA annual forecast of [[p84_value]] against the [[p558_value]] total, month-over-month seasonality, and a BEV/non-BEV split using [[p9_value]] and [[p34_value]].

All inputs are observed historical or current-year figures; the September 2026 outcome is a transfer from them. The combination is the median of five equally weighted blocks, with overlapping inputs grouped rather than treated as independent. The main risk is that only two historical Septembers inform seasonality and that working-day and holiday timing distort the ratios. Actual September 2026 daily registration data would most improve the estimate.

Unit of the estimate: [[unit_full]].

Key assumptions: none (every formula input is an observed data point).

Method details (computed by code):
- m1 formula_mc: p297 * mean(p1 / (p2 - p1), p45 / (p46 - p45)); Monte Carlo P10 to P90 [[m1_mc_p10]] to [[m1_mc_p90]]; result unit vehicle converted to vehicle; own 80% width [[m1_width]] (no error evidence, code's default width)
- m2 formula_mc: p1 * (1 + mean(p475, p31)); Monte Carlo P10 to P90 [[m2_mc_p10]] to [[m2_mc_p90]]; result unit (vehicle/month) * 1 month converted to vehicle; own 80% width [[m2_width]] (no error evidence, code's default width)
- m3 formula_mc: p1 * (p84 / p558); Monte Carlo P10 to P90 [[m3_mc_p10]] to [[m3_mc_p90]]; result unit (vehicle/month) * 1 month converted to vehicle; own 80% width [[m3_width]] (no error evidence, code's default width)
- m4 formula_mc: p30 * (1 + mean(p4, p48)); Monte Carlo P10 to P90 [[m4_mc_p10]] to [[m4_mc_p90]]; result unit (vehicle/month) * 1 month converted to vehicle; own 80% width [[m4_width]] (no error evidence, code's default width)
- m5 formula_mc: p9 * (1 + p34) + (p1 - p9) * ((p30 - p32) / (p30 / (1 + p31) - p32 / (1 + p34))); Monte Carlo P10 to P90 [[m5_mc_p10]] to [[m5_mc_p90]]; result unit (vehicle/month) * 1 month converted to vehicle; own 80% width [[m5_width]] (no error evidence, code's default width)
- Combination: [[n_blocks]] block(s), equal weight per block (methods whose inputs overlap by at least half form one block; backtest errors set widths, not weights): B1 = m1: [[block1_value]] (width [[block1_width]], no error evidence, code's default width); B2 = m2: [[block2_value]] (width [[block2_width]], no error evidence, code's default width); B3 = m3: [[block3_value]] (width [[block3_width]], no error evidence, code's default width); B4 = m4: [[block4_value]] (width [[block4_width]], no error evidence, code's default width); B5 = m5: [[block5_value]] (width [[block5_width]], no error evidence, code's default width). Estimate = the median of the blocks.
- Interval: root mean square of the block widths [[blocks_rms_width]]; Birge ratio [[birge_ratio]] (not above one, so no widening); final width [[final_width]].
final.text:
The best estimate for new passenger car (Pkw) registrations in Germany during September 2026 is 239,315 vehicle (80% model-based interval 173,711 to 329,695 vehicle). This covers domestic new Pkw registration events counted by the KBA for the full month, not sales, orders, or production.

Evidence: September 2025 was 235,528 new passenger car (Pkw) registration; January–August 2026 cumulative was 1,965,024 new passenger car (Pkw) registration; August 2026 was 212,563 new passenger car (Pkw) registration with year-on-year growth of 2.6%. Routes apply historical September shares, recent momentum, a VDA annual forecast of 2,900,000 new passenger car (Pkw) registration against the 2,857,591 new passenger car (Pkw) registration total, month-over-month seasonality, and a BEV/non-BEV split using 45,495 new passenger car (Pkw) registration and 75.1%.

All inputs are observed historical or current-year figures; the September 2026 outcome is a transfer from them. The combination is the median of five equally weighted blocks, with overlapping inputs grouped rather than treated as independent. The main risk is that only two historical Septembers inform seasonality and that working-day and holiday timing distort the ratios. Actual September 2026 daily registration data would most improve the estimate.

Unit of the estimate: vehicle (new passenger car (Pkw) registration; total for 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-30).

Key assumptions: none (every formula input is an observed data point).

Method details (computed by code):
- m1 formula_mc: p297 * mean(p1 / (p2 - p1), p45 / (p46 - p45)); Monte Carlo P10 to P90 177,172 to 311,260; result unit vehicle converted to vehicle; own 80% width x/÷1.38 (no error evidence, code's default width)
- m2 formula_mc: p1 * (1 + mean(p475, p31)); Monte Carlo P10 to P90 200,343 to 288,652; result unit (vehicle/month) * 1 month converted to vehicle; own 80% width x/÷1.38 (no error evidence, code's default width)
- m3 formula_mc: p1 * (p84 / p558); Monte Carlo P10 to P90 174,508 to 330,380; result unit (vehicle/month) * 1 month converted to vehicle; own 80% width x/÷1.38 (no error evidence, code's default width)
- m4 formula_mc: p30 * (1 + mean(p4, p48)); Monte Carlo P10 to P90 194,548 to 280,442; result unit (vehicle/month) * 1 month converted to vehicle; own 80% width x/÷1.38 (no error evidence, code's default width)
- m5 formula_mc: p9 * (1 + p34) + (p1 - p9) * ((p30 - p32) / (p30 / (1 + p31) - p32 / (1 + p34))); Monte Carlo P10 to P90 206,031 to 285,070; result unit (vehicle/month) * 1 month converted to vehicle; own 80% width x/÷1.38 (no error evidence, code's default width)
- Combination: 5 block(s), equal weight per block (methods whose inputs overlap by at least half form one block; backtest errors set widths, not weights): B1 = m1: 233,938 (width x/÷1.38, no error evidence, code's default width); B2 = m2: 240,176 (width x/÷1.38, no error evidence, code's default width); B3 = m3: 239,315 (width x/÷1.38, no error evidence, code's default width); B4 = m4: 233,367 (width x/÷1.38, no error evidence, code's default width); B5 = m5: 241,774 (width x/÷1.38, no error evidence, code's default width). Estimate = the median of the blocks.
- Interval: root mean square of the block widths x/÷1.38; Birge ratio 0.06 (not above one, so no widening); final width x/÷1.38.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.

The magnitude gate (v2.15d) asks the model once, without retrieval, for a rough estimate; whether the evidence-based estimate is more than 2x above or below it can carry the model's memory of the target into one repair. The rough number itself never enters a computation or a prompt; the estimate before that repair is kept in judge_rounds[-1].magnitude_checks[0]. The gate is off in the own-history ablation.
